newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania says Deutsche Bank to help in bond issue.
newsitem.headline: Romania says Deutsche Bank to help in bond issue.

text.p: Romania's government said that Germany's Deutsche Bank had offered to participate in the launching of government bonds planned for the next two months on world capital markets.
A government statement issued late on Monday said the offer had been made during a meeting between Romanian Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea and visiting Deutsche Bank executives.
Executives of Deutsche Bank, which does not have offices in Romania, could not be contacted for comment.
The statement also said Deutsche Bank had expressed interest in the privatisation of Romanian banks as well as in boosting German investments in Romania.
Last week the Finance Ministry said it planned to issue around 500 million marks in bonds, its first international raising, in about two months.
The ministry invited major investment banks, including CS First Boston, Merrill Lynch, JP Morgan and Deutsche Bank to offer consultancy on the issue.

After an absence of more than a decade, Romania rejoined international capital markets in 1995 with syndicated loans for the National Bank (central bank), which also launched the first Samurai and Eurobond issues last year.

Last year Romania won its first credit ratings from major agencies. Japan Credit Rating agency awarded it a BB-plus, somewhat higher than the BB-minus ratings of Standard and Poor's and IBCA and BA-three from Moody's Investors Service.

Ciorbea's new centrist coalition government, which ousted ex-communists in last November's elections, has announced on a tough reform programme to put the economy on track and and win international financial support.
It also pledged to foster the selloff of five Romanian state banks. The first state bank likely to turn private is Banca Romana pentru Dezvoltare SA.
Ciorbea said his cabinet planned to offer foreign investors up to 90-95 percent of state banks' equity.

The International Monetary Fund is expected to approve a $400 million, one-year stand-by loan in mid-April. The World Bank is also seen lending another $600 million for worker retraining and support for farmers.
Last week parliament's lower house approved a ceiling of $3.2 billion for international loans raised by the central bank and finance ministry this year.
